Recall that $F(x,y)=P(X\le x,Y\le y)$ is the probability that the pair $(X,Y)$ will lie inside the infinite rectangular region that has its top-right corner at $(x,y)$ and whose sides are parallel to the coordinate axes.

Let's sketch the region corresponding to the probability we wish to find.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/foundations/14274884/assets/6d99e5e84349bb1279f4a105a6611b55a85e41aa2bf96e1dc28a8a343e0d9432.png)

Geometrically, this region can be obtained as follows:

1\. Take the infinite rectangle that has its top-right corner at $(10,9).$

2\. Subtract the infinite rectangles that have their top-right corners at $(10,5)$ and $(8,9).$

3\. Finally, we need to *add back* the infinite rectangle that has its top-right corner at $(8,5).$ This is because we subtracted this region twice in step 2.

Therefore, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}P(8\le X\le 10,5\le Y\le 9) & =\overset{\text{top-right corner at }(10,9)}{\overset{⏞}{P(X\le 10,Y\le 9)}} \\  & \,-\overset{\text{top-right corner at }(10,5)}{\overset{⏞}{P(X\le 10,Y\le 5)}}-\overset{\text{top-right corner at }(8,9)}{\overset{⏞}{P(X\le 8,Y\le 9)}} \\  & \,+\overset{\text{top-right corner at }(8,5)}{\overset{⏞}{P(X\le 8,Y\le 5)}} \\  & =F(10,9)-F(10,5)-F(8,9)+F(8,5) \\  & =0.7-0.2-0.3+0.1 \\  & =0.3.\end{aligned}
$$
